I traced the runTool refactor and it keeps the same behavior:
- Arguments, stdin /dev/null and stderr discarded are all still set, now inside BoundedProcess.run.
- SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 1 s later, is the same sequence.
- The race-window case (child finished right at the deadline) accepted exactly this: drained, not running, terminationReason .exit, status 0. That is what Outcome.exitedCleanly checks now.
- The drain timeout when the child had already exited used to throw timedOut. It now sets timedOut = !drainedInTime, exitedCleanly is false, and it still throws Failure.timedOut.
- A launch error still maps to Failure.launchFailed, and a non-zero status to Failure.exited.

The credential fallback contract in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md:551 (exact-match arguments, stdin /dev/null, stderr discarded, 5 s budget that kills the child, cooldown, readOffPool, never used for writes) still describes the code accurately. The existing SecurityToolCredentialReaderTests suite is untouched. It keeps covering the reader's behavior across the refactor.

Public surface: BoundedProcess is a new public enum in Core. It is needed because the App target (DMGVerifier.swift:114-121) consumes it. new_findings: INFO (SCOPE/tests): BoundedProcessTests starts real /bin/sh and /bin/sleep children with a 0.3 s budget and asserts timing under 5-6 s. It depends on the host, the same way the round-1 hdiutil tests do. That is fine on macOS runners, but it could flake on a very overloaded CI machine.

INFO (SCOPE/API): BoundedProcess.Outcome.status is 0 when terminationReason is nil (the child survived the SIGKILL wait). Both callers check timedOut before they read status, so no wrong result escapes today. A future caller that reads status alone would see a false 0. Consider making status optional in a follow-up.
